title: Gemini API and SDK Workflows
summary: This intermediate module enables learners to evaluate the documentation needed for a Gemini API or SDK workflow without inventing implementation details. After completing it, learners can distinguish established information from UNKNOWN information and identify what must be verified before implementing a request.
objectives: Identify the first-party documentation areas that must be reviewed before implementing a Gemini API or SDK workflow.
Explain why package names, configuration keys, model identifiers, request methods, and response fields must not be inferred when current documentation is unavailable.
Record the unresolved source change and describe which implementation material remains affected.
Prepare a verification checklist for a future documentation review.

sections.title: Level and scope
paragraphs: This is an intermediate module. It assumes that you can read API documentation, recognize a structured request and response, and evaluate a short programming example. It does not assume prior knowledge of a particular Gemini SDK, package, model, endpoint, or configuration mechanism.

The Gemini API is the named Google API covered by the cited Google documentation. Exact SDK names, supported languages, package names, versions, installation commands, configuration keys, model identifiers, endpoint paths, request methods, payload fields, response properties, limits, and error behavior are UNKNOWN because the referenced documentation could not be retrieved during this update. Those details are therefore omitted.
sections.callout: Do not turn remembered examples into current instructions. Retrieve and inspect the first-party documentation before selecting any implementation detail.

sections.title: Source change and affected material
paragraphs: The existing item cited content/modules/google-gemini-practice/gemini-api-and-sdk-workflows.json as an unregistered source that had never been verified. That path is a repository file path rather than an HTTPS documentation source.

The correction was triggered because a cited source moved or exceeded its review cadence. Which event occurred, the prior source URL, its canonical replacement, and the guidance that changed are UNKNOWN because the existing module and its source records were not supplied.

This unresolved source change affects every implementation statement that would depend on current Gemini documentation, including SDK selection, installation, authentication configuration, model selection, request construction, response handling, and migration guidance. No claim about those details is made here.

Material unaffected by the change cannot be identified or reproduced because the previous module text is unavailable. Preserving an exact minimal diff requires the repository version of the file at the update base commit.

sections.title: Documentation review workflow
paragraphs: Begin with the Gemini API documentation overview to establish the documented product scope. Then inspect the quickstart for the exact workflow presented to new users. Use the generation reference to confirm request and response mechanisms rather than inferring field names or payload shapes.

Inspect the libraries documentation before choosing an SDK. If an existing implementation is being updated, inspect the migration documentation as well. A migration review must determine whether library recommendations, package identities, initialization patterns, or API calls changed.

For every implementation detail, record the exact first-party page that establishes it and the date on which that page was successfully retrieved and reviewed. If the page cannot be retrieved, mark the detail UNKNOWN and omit it from executable instructions.

sections.title: Implementation verification checklist
paragraphs: Before writing an API example, verify the documented endpoint or request method, authentication mechanism, model identifier, input structure, response structure, relevant metadata, limits, and error behavior.
Before writing an SDK example, additionally verify the supported language, recommended SDK name, package name, installation command, initialization pattern, and method used for the request.

After verification, compare the resulting guidance with the previous module line by line. Change only statements affected by the moved or overdue source. This comparison cannot be completed for the present update because the previous file contents are UNKNOWN.

A learner who previously had only the module title can now identify the documentation required for a supported workflow, isolate details that remain UNKNOWN, and avoid publishing guessed configuration or code.

sections.title: Verification status
paragraphs: The cited Google URLs were identified as candidate first-party sources and checked on 2026-08-22, but network retrieval was unavailable. Their content, redirects, and canonical status could not be verified during drafting.

A complete correction requires successful retrieval of the cited pages, the previous JSON file, the previous source records, and the catalogue registry. The registry is needed to confirm catalogue-wide uniqueness of the module and question identifiers.

questions.prompt: What is known about the source change that triggered this update?
choices: A specific SDK package was renamed.
A cited source moved or exceeded its review cadence, but the specific event and changed guidance are UNKNOWN.
questions.explanation: The source-change section states that the trigger was a moved or overdue source, while the prior URL, specific event, and affected guidance remain UNKNOWN.

questions.prompt: What should happen when a current package name or configuration key cannot be established from retrieved first-party documentation?
choices: Use the most familiar remembered value.
Infer it from an unrelated SDK.
Mark it UNKNOWN and omit it from executable instructions.
Create a plausible placeholder without labeling it.
questions.explanation: The module directs learners to mark an unverified detail UNKNOWN and omit it rather than turning memory or inference into current instructions.

questions.prompt: Which documentation areas does the module say to inspect before selecting or migrating an SDK?
choices: The libraries documentation and, for an existing implementation, the migration documentation
questions.explanation: The documentation-review workflow directs learners to inspect the libraries documentation before SDK selection and the migration documentation when updating an existing implementation.

questions.prompt: What is required to verify that an update changes only material affected by the source change?
choices: A remembered version of the old guidance
The previous file at the update base commit for a line-by-line comparison
questions.explanation: The module states that preserving and demonstrating a minimal diff requires the previous repository version for line-by-line comparison.
